description: MimiPAGE2009.jl implements the PAGE09 integrated climate-economy assessment model in Julia. Its public GitHub README says the equations were reconstructed from the published PAGE description and checked against the original spreadsheet version. The model accepts emissions and socioeconomic assumptions, simulates climate-related damages and supports estimates such as the social cost of carbon. It can be used to compare climate-policy or energy-transition scenarios at broad scales. It is not an engineering model of a particular grid, pipeline or building; any infrastructure interpretation needs another system model. The repository gives setup instructions for Julia 1.6 or newer and GitHub reports an MIT licence. The Scientific Data descriptor describes validation against the original model, while a separate Zenodo archive holds replication material. I read the own repository metadata and README but did not install Julia or reproduce model outputs. No exact catalogue record was found. Its coverage is global climate and economic impacts, not site-level infrastructure dynamics.
